content.comment_body: I'm hoping for some help with my first [product_name] and [product_name] operator device. I am unable to transfer data from my Windows 7 PC. I repeatedly get an error stating the PC and the controller are on different subnets and it's unable to connect. My PC address is 192.168.1.77, the controller's address is 192.168.0.201, and the operator device is at 192.168.0.2. Thank you.

The controller, operator device, and PC all need to be within the same IP address range. IP addresses have four segments (www.xxx.yyy.zzz); the first three segments should match for all devices, and only the final segment should differ. Also, ensure all devices share the same subnet mask, like 255.255.255.0.

Thanks [user_name]. I am still facing an issue, so I'm testing with just the [product_name] connected to my PC. The PC uses 192.168.0.4, while the controller is at 192.168.0.201. These addresses were initially set by the operator device before disconnecting it. The subnet mask is 255.255.255.0. The default gateway field is blank in my PC’s LAN settings. I've removed antivirus software, disabled WiFi, and connected the patch cable only between the laptop and controller. I've searched Google all day, and would appreciate any guidance. Thanks.

Thanks again, I now have connectivity with the [product_name] controller. I wasn't aware of network protocol specifics, but your guidance helped a lot. The primary issue was not paying full attention to the Help documentation about the interface. After clearing the target IP box, the correct address populated automatically; aligning my PC's network properties resolved everything. As the saying goes, 'If all else fails, read the instructions.' Thanks.
There's definitely value in reviewing instructions ahead of time.

Lack of clarity around required network settings for the PC, controller, and operator device led to initial confusion. The issue was resolved after understanding the need for matching network configurations and by referencing Help documentation.
